items: Liveness and readiness on the SAME endpoint
And that endpoint checks downstream dependencies
DB blips, every Pod's liveness fails at once
kubelet restarts the entire Deployment together
Cluster-wide CrashLoopBackOff while the DB is still down

blocks.title: The correct split
blocks.text: Liveness = shallow, only 'my process and event loop are alive'. Readiness = may check dependencies. Liveness must NEVER touch a database or another service.

items: timeoutSeconds defaults to 1 second
A GC pause or CPU throttle blows through it
Spurious restarts get blamed on 'flaky Kubernetes'
Throttled, slow, liveness kill, restart, throttled again
Restart-loop root cause is often the CPU limit
requests are for the SCHEDULER, not the runtime
They say how much capacity to reserve
The scheduler uses them when picking a node
limits are for the KERNEL on that node
cgroups enforce them as a hard runtime ceiling
CPU 1 = one core, vCPU or hyperthread
500m = 0.5 core; m means millicores
Mi and Gi are binary units
1Mi is exactly 1048576 bytes
M and G are decimal, about 5% smaller
Mixing the two is a classic sizing error

blocks.title: Write Mi, never M
blocks.text: A manifest that says 512M gives you 488Mi of real memory. Five percent sounds harmless until it is the five percent your heap needed.

items: Set requests from observed p50 to p90 usage
Set the memory limit near the request
Think hard before setting a CPU limit at all
CPU limits throttle; memory limits kill

blocks.title: Autoscaler coupling
items: VPA recommends or sets values from history
HPA scales replica count off utilization
Utilization is measured against the REQUEST
A wrong request miscalibrates your autoscaler silently

blocks.title: The request is the unit of truth
blocks.text: Both schedulers and HPA reason about the request, not real usage. Guess it high and you waste a node; guess it low and the autoscaler thinks you are on fire at half load.

items: Assigned automatically, never set directly
Guaranteed: limits equal requests, every container
Burstable: requests set, limits higher or missing
BestEffort: no requests and no limits at all
The kubelet watches the node, not your Pod
It tracks memory.available on the node
It tracks nodefs.available for the disk
It tracks imagefs.available for image storage
Each is compared against an eviction threshold
Cross it and the kubelet evicts Pods to reclaim
BestEffort Pods are evicted first
Then Burstable Pods exceeding their requests
Those rank by how far over they are
Guaranteed Pods are evicted last
Inside a tier, higher priority is evicted later
An evicted Pod shows reason: Evicted
An OOMKilled container shows exit code 137
describe node shows the pressure conditions

blocks.title: Eviction is not OOMKill
items: OOMKill: the kernel hit your memory limit
Eviction: the kubelet reclaimed a pressured node
Eviction is graceful; OOMKill never is

blocks.title: Requests buy survival
blocks.text: Staying under your request is what moves you down the kill list. A BestEffort Pod is free to schedule and first to die.

items: Some runtimes size the heap from host memory
The host has 64Gi; your limit is 512Mi
The heap grows past the cgroup limit
OOMKill lands before you serve one request
Use container-aware flags, not host guesses
-XX:MaxRAMPercentage reads the cgroup limit
Keep headroom for non-heap memory
Threads, metaspace and buffers live outside the heap

blocks.title: Heap is not the container
blocks.text: Size the heap to a percentage of the limit, never to the limit itself. The rest of the process still needs room to exist.

items: Set minAvailable or maxUnavailable, pick one
It protects against VOLUNTARY disruption only
Node drains and cluster autoscaler scale-down
It does NOT stop OOMKills or node crashes
It does NOT stop node-pressure eviction
Mutating a ConfigMap without versioning its name
Mounted files update eventually, up to a minute
Env vars from a ConfigMap never update
Nothing restarts your Pods either way
Version the name or add a checksum annotation
Setting replicas in a manifest an HPA manages
Every kubectl apply fights the autoscaler
Remove spec.replicas when an HPA owns it

blocks.title: Own it once
blocks.text: Every field needs exactly one owner. Version your ConfigMap names, and let the HPA own replica count alone.

items: requests = scheduler reservation
limits = kernel ceiling
CPU throttles, memory kills
Requests set from real p50 to p90 usage
Memory limit near the request, written in Mi
A CPU limit only with a reason you can state
Heap flags read the cgroup, not the host
HPA target measured against a sane request
spec.replicas absent when an HPA owns it
ConfigMap name versioned or checksum annotated
PDB set, knowing what it cannot protect

blocks.title: Three ways a Pod dies
items: OOMKill: kernel hit your memory limit
Eviction: kubelet reclaimed a pressured node
Drain: voluntary, and a PDB can slow it
Measure a week of real traffic first
Set requests at p90, not at peak
Watch throttling and OOMKill counters after
Re-measure; sizing is never a one-time task

blocks.title: Measure, then size
blocks.text: Every number on this page comes from observation, not from a template. Copy a colleague's limits and you inherit their incidents.
